title: Krull dimension does not increase on an open subspace
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $U'\subseteq U\subseteq X$ be open subsets, each with its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Then $\dim(U')\leq\dim(U)$ for the Krull dimensions of these topological spaces [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Topology, Section 'Krull dimension', remark immediately after Definition 0055 (label definition-Krull), lines 1421-1425: if U' subset U subset X are open then dim(U') <= dim(U)

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: for U' ⊆ U (h : U' ⊆ U as Set X), the inclusion Set.inclusion h : U' → U is an embedding, hence inducing (Topology.IsEmbedding.inclusion h, Mathlib/Topology/Constructions.lean:598), so (Topology.IsEmbedding.inclusion h).isInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le : topologicalKrullDim U' ≤ topologicalKrullDim U. topologicalKrullDim is exactly the Krull dimension of def-kun-topological-krull-dimension (its Mathlib leaf, with ⊥ = -∞ for the empty space, ⊤ = ∞), and subtypes carry the subspace topology of def-kun-subspace-topology. Openness of U, U' is not needed.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Topology, remark after Definition 0055 (tag 0055 = topology-definition-Krull verified in tags/tags; topology.tex lines 1421-1425): correct, kept. stmt_deps kept. The earlier searches had judged Mathlib's topologicalKrullDim inequalities 'related but not a match' because of a supposed difference of convention; but def-kun-topological-krull-dimension is itself the exact Mathlib leaf topologicalKrullDim (supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets, ⊥ for empty) and def-kun-subspace-topology is the subtype topology, so Topology.IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le applied to the embedding Set.inclusion h : U' → U (Topology.IsEmbedding.inclusion) is the statement in one line, even without openness.
